subtallies.name: Four defensible denominators
cells: any tree that owns attributes anywhere (revision 1 — wrong: counts eBay/Shopee/Tokopedia B as declining something they cannot express)
internal nodes own a per-node schema (like-for-like with D15)

framing: The unanimity is narrower than “nothing flows”, and the denominator has to be derived: inheritance is only expressible where an internal node owns a schema. eBay is the direct evidence for “per kind of fact” — the fact it attaches only to leaves (aspects) it does not inherit; the fact it attaches to every node (category features) it does, explicitly, with override and a published wire format. Our own code already carries six kinds of category-derived fact resolved by four mechanisms.

rows.h: no tree on the attribute owner
rows.shape: “No tree on the attribute owner — ProductType has exactly 3 properties; set materialised per product type as one JSON Schema per call.” Browse-node refinements: 219 of 237 parent→child pairs superset, 18 not. “No mechanism named; the meta-schema vocabulary is 12 keywords, none an override or exclusion keyword.” (First-party 2026-09-21: the meta-schema page lists editable, enumNames, hidden, maxUniqueItems, minUniqueItems, maxUtf8ByteLength, minUtf8ByteLength, selectors, $lifecycle, replacedBy, replaces, enumDeprecated — none an inheritance keyword.)

rows.h: internal nodes DO own schemas (97.8 %) and the child often drops — a real “no”
rows.shape: “No — materialised per node and the child often drops: 4,668 of 14,580 pairs in the published v2026-08 file, 4,877 measured live. "inherit → 0 in 95,136,132 B.” “Not inheritance; the child's own list is authoritative. Enforced at write” — the same mutation succeeded on the parent's product and was refused on the child's: “Owner subtype does not match the metafield definition's constraints.” Live 2026-09-21: Flavor on Snack Foods (L3) and its child Snack Cakes (L4), but Chocolate (L4) carries Chocolate type that Candy & Chocolate need not.

rows.h: two kinds of fact, two answers — the direct evidence for per-kind
rows.shape: Aspects: “leaf-only and self-contained.” Category features: yes, explicitly — “‘override’ is eBay's own word and the wire format is built on it.”

rows.h: + an enumerated exception list for requiredness
rows.shape: “No per-node set exists — one global ProductAttributes bag; 5 methods, none takes a category.” “Yes for requiredness — 16 named Apparel sub-categories are Optional where ancestor 166 is Required, as an enumerated prose exception list.”

“No tree on the attribute owner — 6,967 sibling PT keys in one flat map, $ref = 0 across 451,013,258 B; materialised in full per PT.” “No child node exists; every PT and Visible carry "additionalProperties": false.”
“No inheritance mechanism at all — 0 hits across 1,704,281 B + 3,302,641 B.” No override, because no inheritance.

Era A: axes come from get_variant?cat_id= after step 1 returns a leaf id; no inheritance mechanism named. Era B: “Bound to one leaf category; no mechanism named. Non-leaf nodes cannot be queried for attributes at all.”

rows.h: for attributes; forced inheritance for one other fact
rows.shape: “No per-category attribute set exists; the only gate is allowed_object_types.” For online_visibility the child could not hold a differing value — the parent's write rewrote the child row, same updated_at to the millisecond (observed three ways, stated in no vendor text).

“Yes — the model is the union of global groups + the classification category's groups + ‘any parent categories’ of it.” Override by id collision: “the sub-category group overrides the parent group.” Removal of a group is never stated.

rows.h: on a different object — the Family tree, SaaS only
rows.shape: “Yes on the Family tree, SaaS only — the vendor names it ‘Attribute Inheritance’. Category tree: none. FamilyVariant levels hold disjoint sets: values flow, definitions do not.” Cannot remove an inherited attribute while linked (workaround: detach → edit parent → re-attach); completeness requirements cannot be overridden.

“Neither — a product_cat term carries no attribute definitions … 514 lines contain product_cat; 0 also contain attribute_taxonom.” Unset display_type/thumbnail_id fall back to a site option, never the parent.
“ProductType is flat — its property list has no parent, ancestors or children. The Category tree owns no attribute definitions.” Nothing inherited on either object.

“No for the category tree — attribute sets are flat (4 columns, no parent); 0 of 63 Catalog tables join a category to a product attribute.” Per node for category EAV (is_anchor, custom_use_parent_settings); attribute-set “Based On” copies once with no standing link.
